exclude: The fixed 32-page copy runs past the end of this island file. The authored payload is listed up to the file length.
Outside the suffix-2 file. This tail of the staging window can still contain the suffix-1 file, which is listed at its installed address.
Runtime copy of the tile and palette bytes installed by $0F57. The disk bytes are listed in the staging window.
Installed copy of the six character pages at $9800-$9DFF. List the source bytes once.
Runtime sprite slots expanded by the loop at $0F9D. The source images and all the expansion tables are listed at $9F05 and above.

comments.text: Low bytes of the 32 type-indexed script pointers for island 5. $685E copies this field into the object slot at $09E0,X.
High bytes of the type-indexed script pointers for island 5. Entries pointing below $1B00 use shared scripts in the resident engine.
Initial type and flags loaded at $680A. The full byte goes to $08F0,X and the high nibble also goes to $0900,X.
Type $0F flags can be patched at $62AD. The following bytes initialize the same flags for types $10 through $1F.
Type-indexed field copied to $0B00,X at $681B. Its sign controls whether a slot is skipped during the mode checked by $6A81.
Type-indexed byte copied to $0B41,X at $6815. $62A8 can overwrite entry $0F for the current game state.
Initial frame for type $0F, patched at $62A8. The remainder supplies the initial frame for types $10 through $1F.
Low bytes of four round setup tables, selected by $4B modulo four at $4ED4.
High bytes of the four round setup tables. $4EE5 copies one 256-byte table to $0200.
Round and section indexed values loaded into $15 and $A0 by $4258. The same byte seeds $17 minus four and $18 plus 22.
Scroll origins for section indices one and two, immediately after the first entry at $1BA8.
Used at $427D after X is masked with $FC. This point is the fourth entry in the first group of four, followed by the other groups.
Initial player Y values indexed by round group and section. $4269 reads the value and $426C writes it to slot zero at $0970.
Screen and object Y values at index three and later. $6390 uses the entries separated by four to seed an item position four rows below the corresponding boundary.
Section-indexed bytes copied into $76 at $426F for the chosen round group.
Section rows read by $4274 and kept in $90.
Read by $6517 and $726A. This byte immediately precedes the first local object script.
Island 5 object script entry for types $10. $6C57 fetches commands using the slot script offset and dispatches through $0DB1 and $0DF1.
Island 5 object script entry for types $13. $6C57 fetches commands using the slot script offset and dispatches through $0DB1 and $0DF1.

Island 5 object script entry for types $17. $6C57 fetches commands using the slot script offset and dispatches through $0DB1 and $0DF1.
Round 1 setup table for island 5. $4EE5 reads 256 bytes from this pointer and copies them to $0200 before the map is decoded.
Round 2 setup table for island 5. $4EE5 reads 256 bytes from this pointer and copies them to $0200 before the map is decoded.
Round 3 setup table for island 5. $4EE5 reads 256 bytes from this pointer and copies them to $0200 before the map is decoded.
Round 4 setup table for island 5. $4EE5 reads 256 bytes from this pointer and copies them to $0200 before the map is decoded.
Group count at $2101 and high-byte-first boundary pairs. $4FCB subtracts adjacent boundaries to get the counts used when setting bits in the decoded table at $9000.
Number of variable-length dictionary groups. $4F6E doubles this count to index the final offset and $4FCB uses it as the initial group index.
High byte of the first dictionary boundary. $4FD8 and $4FDB subtract neighboring words.
Low byte of the first boundary and source of the group-flag mask loaded at $4FEB.
High-byte base of the boundary table indexed by twice the group number.
Low-byte base of the dictionary boundaries. $4F76 adds one to the final boundary's low byte before decoding.
Four high-byte-first offsets from $2100. $505C and $5062 position the bit reader at the stream for the chosen round.
Low byte of the first round stream offset. $5062 reads this side of each big-endian pair indexed by twice the round.
High-byte-first offset from $2100 to the compressed dictionary stream. The loader initializes the stream with $5230 and writes groups of four bytes to $9000.
Low byte used as X by $4F61 when positioning the map bit reader on the dictionary.
Five high-byte-first boundaries. $502E and $5038 use the selected round boundary to calculate the first row and destination in the decoded map at $9800.
Low byte of the start boundary read by $502E. Later pairs hold the other round boundaries.

Bit streams for island 5. $5246 shifts a common seed from $2128 and fetches subsequent bytes at the dictionary and round stream offsets. The setup code writes the decoded dictionary at $9000 and the expanded map at $9800.
Interior of the island 5 map data. The self-modifying reader at $525C fetches its next byte through this operand and increments it before each refill.
Island 5 round 1 stream bytes $2428 through $2727. The round decoder consumes this bit stream to write the expanded map at $9800.
Island 5 round 1 stream bytes $2728 through $27DF. The round decoder consumes this bit stream to write the expanded map at $9800.
Island 5 round 2 stream bytes $27E0 through $2ADF. The round decoder consumes this bit stream to write the expanded map at $9800.
Island 5 round 2 stream bytes $2AE0 through $2C99. The round decoder consumes this bit stream to write the expanded map at $9800.
Island 5 round 3 stream bytes $2C9A through $2DC3. The round decoder consumes this bit stream to write the expanded map at $9800.
Island 5 round 4 stream bytes $2DC4 through $30C3. The round decoder consumes this bit stream to write the expanded map at $9800.
Map stream bytes at an address that holds the attract routine while Island 1 is loaded. The transition to the title restores Island 1 before calling $2F00.
Island 5 round 4 stream bytes $30C4 through $338B. The round decoder consumes this bit stream to write the expanded map at $9800.
Island 5 dictionary stream bytes $338C through $368B. The decoder reads paired 11-bit values from this stream for the output at $9000.
Island 5 dictionary stream bytes $368C through $394C. The decoder reads paired 11-bit values from this stream for the output at $9000.
First 128 of the 192 eight-byte character images for island 5. $0F57 copies six pages into the VIC-II character area at $C800.
Characters $80 through $BF of the island 5 tile set. The setup loop installs these final two pages at $CC00 and $CD00.
One page copied to both $CE00 and $0600 by $0F75. The two copies support the screen tile and colour routines.
First five bytes of the six-byte setup copied to $0700. $4F14 uses byte 0 to patch $76DD and the next three bytes to choose background colours.
Byte dictionary used by $0FBD when a sprite slot is marked for expansion. The source record supplies the byte index as Y.
Dictionary entries $FB through $FF, covering the last five possible source-byte indexes used by $0FBD.
One byte per destination sprite slot. A nonzero byte uses the direct 63-byte copy at $0FCD. Zero uses the byte dictionary and the offset map.
Low bytes of 64 sprite source pointers, installed in the source instructions at $0FBA and $0FCD.
High bytes of 64 sprite source pointers, used by both the direct and dictionary copy paths.
63 destination offsets used with dictionary-expanded sprite bytes. The direct copy path preserves the original byte order.
